findings.detail: The question has the same problem as M2-S41-T2. Both are set in a CI pull-request review where style remarks crowd out real defects, and both ask for the fix. In both, the correct answer is to define categories to report (bugs, security) and categories to skip (minor style), and the same reasoning leads there. The new detail, that a confidence line was already tried and failed, does not change the choice. M4-S09-T2 already covers why such a line fails. Wrong option A here (a stronger general instruction) also repeats the 'be conservative' distractor of M2-S41-T2.

blind_answer.reason: Confidence-based filtering cut true bugs and style noise alike, so precision did not improve (4.1-K2). Explicit categorical criteria fix this (4.1-S1): report bugs and security flaws, skip minor style. Option A makes the same filter stricter. Option C relies on self-reported confidence, which is uncalibrated. Option D keeps the flawed confidence line and only patches the one missed bug pattern.
